p: trembleth: At the marvelling of the thunder and lightnings: by which he declares that the faithful are lively touched with the majesty of God, when they behold his works.
noise of his voice: That is the thunder, by which he speaks to men to waken their dullness, and to bring them to the consideration of his works.
them when his voice is heard: Meaning, the rains and thunders.
likewise to the small rain: So that neither small rain nor great, snow nor anything else comes without God's appointment.
sealeth up the hand of every: By rains and thunders God causes men to keep themselves within their houses.
north: In Hebrew it is called the scattering wind, because it drives away the clouds and purges the air.
is straitened: That is, frozen up and dried.
wearieth the thick cloud: Gather the vapours and move to and fro to water the earth.
bright cloud: That is, the cloud that has lightning in it.
correction: Rain, cold, heat, tempests and such like are sent from God, either to punish man, or to profit the earth, or to declare his favour toward man, as in Job 36:31.
light of his cloud to shine: That is, the lightning to break forth in the clouds?
balancings of the clouds: Which is sometimes changed into rain, or snow, hail or such like.
warm: Why your clothes should keep you warm when the south wind blows rather than when any other wind blows?
darkness: That is, our ignorance: signifying that Job was so presumptuous, that he would control the works of God.
told him that I speak: Has God need that any should tell him when man murmurs against him?

which is in the clouds: The cloud stops the shining of the sun, that man cannot see it till the wind has chased away the cloud: and if man is not able to attain to the knowledge of these things, how much less God's judgments?
Fair weather cometh out of the: In Hebrew, gold, meaning fair weather and clear as gold.
